rerecorded.why: Bar-to-bar state. `accum(seed, update, warmup)` is what `var x = 0` / `x := x + 1` needs, and the reason real Pine scripts refused at `pine:state`. The five cases pin the halves that can each break separately -- see `corpus.json::_recurrence`. The property that made it shippable is that the window RE-SEEDS at `i - warmup`: the value at a bar is a function of exactly `warmup + 1` bars, so it cannot change when a chart is panned. A single forward pass from the first fetched bar would have been cheaper, passed every other test in the suite, and disagreed with itself between two requests.

rerecorded.proof: The tool's own reconciliation printed `vs the previous log: 0 MOVED [], 6 added, 0 removed`. Each of the six new cases runs through BOTH lanes over the same 579 bars at the same 1e-9 before it is digested, so the record IS the cross-lane check for them. Three of the six exist because the two host languages disagree BY DEFAULT and would each have looked internally consistent: JS rounds a half toward +inf, Python rounds it to even and Pine rounds it away from zero; `Math.sign(-0)` is -0 while `copysign(1, -0.0)` is -1.0; and `math.floor` RAISES on NaN where `Math.floor` returns it. All three are written out in both walkers rather than inherited.

rerecorded.why: FIX ROUND 1, FINDING 1: `sessionfirst` declared a property that was FALSE. It compares this bar's ET calendar day against the PREVIOUS bar's, so it is a function of TWO bars exactly as `change(close)` is — and it declared `lookback: 0`, with both linters hardcoding a matching zero for every clock name. Two authorities agreeing on one false statement. The measurable cost was that the leading bar of ANY window answered 1 whether or not it opened a session: `bars[1:]` and `bars[4:]` both read [1,0,1,0] where the full series read [0,0,1,0], so the value depended on where the series happened to start rather than on the tape. It now declares `lookback: 1`, both linters derive a clock leaf's reach from that declaration through the same `own_window` a function's reach uses, and the oldest bar is BLANK — the same warm-up pad every windowed entry in this table carries. That blank is the moved digest. The five 0/1 clock entries also went `yields: "num"` -> `"bool"` in the same round, but `yields` is not part of a digest and no other case's column moved.
